subject: Strategic PR support — scope & consolidation options
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara@monarchpr.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood PR scope & options heading into 2027

Hi Monica —

Hope you're well. With end-of-year planning kicking off I wanted to share a short readout on how Monarch PR performed for Redwood in Q3 and propose three engagement options for 2027 so you can evaluate what fits best with the product & events roadmap.

Attached: PR_Perf_Summary_Q3.xlsx (quick metrics: coverage volume, share of voice, top placements), and Monarch_SOW_v3.pdf (redlined SOW with retainer + event add-ons).

High level options we suggest:
- Baseline retainer (current scope, smaller concierge for launches) — predictable coverage, lowest out-of-pocket spend.
- Growth retainer + events (adds two major event activations and crisis support) — better tradeoff for reaching enterprise accounts.
- Consolidated model (we propose folding creative/event comms into a single delivery with a dedicated project manager) — higher up-front cost but ~18% savings vs. separate vendors.

Can you share how you're thinking about consolidation versus tactical renewals? If useful, James from SignalHouse (copied below on future thread) can provide an apples-to-apples event cost comparison.

Would Monday or Tuesday next week for a 30-min sync work?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Director, Accounts — Monarch PR
attachments: PR_Perf_Summary_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Monarch_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@monarchpr.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood PR scope & options heading into 2027

Sara —

Thanks for the summary and the SOW. Quick context from our side: product launches are heavier in H1 (Feb/May) and we have three planned trade shows (Mar/Apr/Jun). We're leaning toward consolidating suppliers where it reduces coordination overhead but need to validate cost and SLA for live event ops.

A couple of asks before a decision:
1) Can Monarch provide a week-by-week staffing plan for the consolidated model (PM, media lead, events ops) and clarify which deliverables you would own vs. Redwood?
2) If Monarch proposes a bundled price, can you also show a line-item comparison vs. current spend (retainer + separate event vendor)?
3) Please include SLAs for press-response windows and event-day escalation coverage.

Laura — looping you in for procurement side visibility. Marissa — curious about comms team capacity and whether consolidation would simplify content production.

Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara@monarchpr.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood PR scope & options heading into 2027

Monica —

Thanks for the clarity. I've attached Monarch_SOW_v3.pdf with a new appendix (tab "Consol_Staffing") and a cost appendix showing the line-item comparison you asked for. We also added proposed event-day escalation SLAs on page 4 (response within 30 minutes for press-critical issues; dedicated on-call event ops).

If helpful I can put together a one-page summary for leadership that shows the expected 12-month TCO and break-even analysis against separate vendors.

Best,
Sara
attachments: Monarch_SOW_v3.pdf (updated), PR_Perf_Summary_Q3.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood PR scope & options heading into 2027

Folks —

Procurement reviewed the SOW and has flagged three items requiring legal/finance sign-off if we move to the consolidated model:
- Payment terms (Net 45 is preferred; Monarch still proposes Net 30 + milestone payments for events)
- IP clause around embargoed product materials (we want explicit restrictions on reuse)
- Cancellation & force majeure language for in-person event costs

Also ran the numbers against our FY27 budget and the consolidated model nets ~15% savings but front-loads spend in Q1. If we need smoothing, we can ask Monarch for a quarterly payment cadence.

I'll compile a short procurement checklist and a redline request list. Monica, do you want procurement to lead negotiations or have your team drive the business terms?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Procurement | Redwood Inference
attachments: Consolidation_Risk_Notes.docx (stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@monarchpr.com>, contracts@monarchpr.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Strategic PR support — scope & consolidation options

Sara / Monarch contracts team —

Thank you for the updated SOW and the breakdown. Procurement has some specific redlines (Laura will send the formal list), but before legal review we want to confirm two things so we can expedite:
1) Can Monarch commit to Net 45 for the retainer (events can remain milestone-based)?
2) If Monarch accepts the consolidated engagement, will you include a 60-day trial clause that allows Redwood to move back to a modular model with a 30% transition credit on pre-paid event fees?

If yes to both, we will prioritize the SOW for signature and target an MSA execution by Dec 10 to ensure vendor onboarding before the January launch.

Next steps: Laura will send the redline list today; Marissa and Markus will review the communications staffing plan and confirm editorial headcount. Please send updated SOW with payment term and trial-clause confirmations by COB Tuesday 24 Nov.

Appreciate it —
Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: Monarch_SOW_v3.pdf, PR_Perf_Summary_Q3.xlsx
